Arif & Ors. Cnr No.: Dlse-01-009181-2017 1. Ayaz Ahmed (minor) S/o Sh. Razzaque Ahmed R/o Rz-509, street no.25, Badi Masjid Tughlakabad-110019. Through its LR/Father Razzaque Ahmed ..........Petitioner Versus 1. Arif S/o Bashir R/o Village-Pilakhna Post-Pilakhna Khas Tehsil-Dibai,PS- Naraura Distt-Bulandshahar, U.P. ............Driver/Respondent no.1 2. Sh. Nand Kishore Garg S/o Sh. Guru Dayal R/o Dd-726, Dabua Colony Nit Faridabad Haryana. ............Owner/Respondent no.2 3. Iffco Tokio Insurance Company Ltd. Regd. Office: Iffco Sadan C-1, District Center Saket, New Delhi-110017. ............Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Charu by Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2025.08.26 16:54:30 +0530 Mact No:989/17 Ayaz Ahmed v. Arif P.No. 1 Of 20 Bk Date of accident : 01.07.2017 Result of accident : Injury Date of filing of Petition : 07.12.2017 Date of Decision : 26.08.2025 Award 1.
texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Ayaz Ahmed(9 years) suffered grievous injury and fracture in his right leg. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/petitioner. Ayaz Ahmed vs Arif on 26 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87890217/ 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 01.07.2017 at about 04:30 p.m., petitioner/injured Ayaz Ahmed alongwith his father and aunt (mausi) was travelling from Bulandshar to Mirzapur on motorcycle bearing no.DL-3SCS-5600. When they reached near Mirzapur, U.P., a Maruti car bearing no.HR-51AB-8784 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came driven in rash and negligent manner from the opposite direction and hit the motorcycle from front right side. Due to the impact, all three riders on the bike fell and sustained injuries. Petitioner suffered a fracture in his right leg. He was taken to JPN Apex Trauma Center, AIIMS, New Delhi where he remained admitted till 09.07.2017. 3. An FIR no.1267/2017, dated 13.07.2017 was registered u/s 279/338 of IPC at PS Kotwali Dehat, Distt-Bulandshahr, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner and respondent no.3/Iffco Tokio Insurance company is the Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA MACT NO:989/17 Ayaz Ahmed v. Arif GUPTA Date: 2025.08.26 P.No. 2 Of 20 BK 16:54:35 +0530 insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Despite service of notice, Respondent no.1 and 2 did not appear and were proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 16.04.2019. In its reply, respondent no.3 has refuted the occurrence of accident and doubted the claim for the reason of delay in lodging of the FIR. It has been pleaded that the injured was in breach of the condition of policy in as much as the offending vehicle was entrusted for driving to Respondent no.1 who did not have a valid driving licence but only a temporary learner's licence. It has also been pleaded that such petitioner and other two injured were triple riding on the motorcycle without helmet, deduction qua contributory negligence be made. 6. Vide order dated 16.04.2019, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 01.07.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-51AB-8784 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner examined his father Sh. Razzaque Ahmed as PW-1. PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He testified on the lines of the claim petition and deposed that his son Ayaz Ahmed sustained facture in his right leg and was removed to Govt. hospital, Bulandshahr, U.P. from where he was referred to AIIMS Trauma center, Delhi. Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: Ayaz Ahmed vs Arif on 26 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87890217/ 2 2025.08.26 16:54:41 +0530 MACT NO:989/17 Ayaz Ahmed v. Arif P.No. 3 Of 20 BK He was admitted on the date of accident i.e. 01.07.2017 and operated on 06.07.2017 during which a steel rod was inserted in his right leg. He was discharged on 09.07.2017. He again admitted on 10.05.2018 for removal of plates. He was operated on 12.05.2018 and discharged on 15.05.2018. He deposed that minor Ayaz Ahmed is still under treatment at the time of filing his affidavit i.e. 2019. At the time of accident, minor Ayaz was studying in 4 th standard in New Green Field school, Alaknanda, Kalkaji. Due to such accident, petitioner/Ayaz could not join the school for 4 months. He spent Rs.1,50,000/- on petitioner's treatment, Rs.25,000/- on conveyance and Rs.30,000/- each on special diet and attendant. He relied upon copy of FIR as Mark-A, discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/2, medical bills as Ex.PW-1/3, School ID of petitioner as Ex.PW-1/4, Birth certificate of petitioner as Ex.PW-1/5, RC of offending vehicle as Mark-B, NCR of lost RC as Mark-C, insurance policy as Mark-D, Discharge summary of 2nd admission of petitioner as Ex.PW-1/9, Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/10. He was duly cross-examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3. After conclusion of petitioner evidence, insurance company led Respondents' evidence by examining Sh. Mrityunjay, Legal Executive of Iffco Tokio General Insurance company as R-3W-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R-3W-1/A. He relied upon documents i.e. Authority letter as Ex.R-3W-1/1, insurance policy as Ex.R-3W-1/2, learner's licence of driver as Ex.R-3W-1/3, CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.26 16:54:46 +0530 MACT NO:989/17 Ayaz Ahmed v. Arif P.No. 4 Of 20 BK Notice u/O 12 Rule 8 CPC as Ex.R-3W-1/4 and postal receipts as Ex.R-3W-1/5. R-3W-1 was duly cross-examined by counsel for petitioner. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ Ayaz Ahmed vs Arif on 26 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87890217/ 3 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 10. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. Further, driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 13. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T.Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Contro (India) (P) Ltd. And Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 16.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 16.7. 24 . At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
